description: The Bricktown Canal Trail in Oklahoma City is a pedestrian-friendly, paved pathway that runs alongside the mile-long manmade canal through the historic and revitalized Bricktown district. Beginning at Bricktown River Walk Park, the trail winds through a mix of restored warehouses, restaurants, bars, public art, and entertainment venues, making it a vibrant urban route. As you stroll, you’ll pass the Chickasaw Bricktown Ballpark and be able to explore attractions like miniature golf, sculptures, and the stunning Centennial Fountain. The canal walk is lined with thoughtfully landscaped green spaces, trees, benches, and scenic bridges, creating a pleasant environment for a leisurely walk or jog. An extension under Interstate 40 and active railroad tracks leads south to Regatta Park and the Oklahoma River Trail, providing the option to continue your journey along the riverfront. The path is suitable for stroller-friendly walking and connects seamlessly to broader trail networks. Popular activities along the trail include casual strolling, people-watching, and dining at canal-side patios. Water taxis offer guided 40-minute rides, giving a different viewpoint of the canal and bringing a historical and entertaining dimension to your visit. Parking is available at Regatta Park and nearby garages by the ballpark, making access convenient. Overall, the Bricktown Canal Trail is an easy, scenic urban loop—about two miles in length when combined with its riverfront connection—offering a blend of waterfront charm, city culture, and recreational convenience.
